sights.w: Contemporary regional art in the 1846 Grubb Mansion — the most intact Greek Revival townhouse in Lancaster County — beside Musser Park.
Judge John Vandersloot's 1908–12 Arts-and-Crafts cabin above the Susquehanna, built as a memorial and museum to Native American culture, with thousands of artifacts set into its walls.

sights.address: Zimmerman Center, 1706 Long Level Rd, Wrightsville, PA 17368
sights.w: Where Union militia burned the mile-long covered bridge on June 28, 1863 to stop Confederates crossing the Susquehanna — the farthest east Lee's army reached. Today's 1930 concrete-arch bridge is an ASCE landmark; the riverside Zimmerman Center is the visitor station for the Captain John Smith Chesapeake National Historic Trail.

sights.address: Front St & Sayford St, Harrisburg, PA 17102
sights.w: Harrisburg's 1912 City Beautiful riverfront — miles of Susquehanna promenade, steps and gardens along Front Street — named one of America's Great Public Spaces by the American Planning Association; the Holocaust Memorial for the Commonwealth (1994) stands at Sayford Street.

A 1,700-sq-ft model railroad of Lancaster County in miniature — 22 operating trains and 150-plus hand-built animations, including tiny Dutch Wonderland and Strasburg Rail Road — grown from the Groff family's 1945 Christmas layout and open to the public since 1961.

Milton Hershey's Depression-era (1933) Mediterranean-style grand hotel on Pat's Hill above the chocolate factory — famous for its circular dining room, built so no guest would be seated in a corner ('if you don't tip well, they put you in a corner'). A Historic Hotels of America member.

sights.address: PA Route 616, Hanover Junction (North Codorus Twp), PA 17362
sights.w: The restored junction depot on the Heritage Rail Trail where Lincoln changed trains en route to deliver the Gettysburg Address in November 1863; small museum of Civil War images and station history.

Lancaster's 80-acre city park at Route 30 and Harrisburg Pike — free Sunday-evening Summer Music Series in the amphitheater since 1962, and the juried Labor Day Art Festival (200-plus exhibitors) since 1979.
